subject: Telemetry scrub validation playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Telemetry scrub validation playbook & next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Recap (what we heard)
- CareBridge wants request/response logging for debugging + audit, but must avoid storing direct PII (names, SSNs, patient identifiers) in logs.
- Key concerns: sensitive headers (trace IDs, auth tokens), data residency for logs (US-only), retention window (target ~90 days), and proof that redaction doesn't break replay/debug flows.
- You asked whether Redwood can: mask/hide trace IDs while preserving linkability for debugging (e.g., hashed IDs), redact headers at ingest, and optionally deliver sanitized audit streams to a customer VPC.

What we can offer (high level)
- Configurable header filters: drop, redact, or hash header values at ingest. Hashing preserves consistent, non-reversible tokens for cross-request correlation.
- Request/response field redaction rules (path + body parsers) and a sanitization audit trail so we can show before/after samples without exposing raw PII.
- Private delivery: sanitized telemetry can be pushed to a customer-owned S3 or kept in your VPC (Redwood Private) for regulated workloads.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a small sample (1–3 days) of request/response logs with sensitive fields redacted or tokenized? We only need examples of header shapes, common error payloads, and a couple of trace IDs to validate hashing behavior. Attach as CSV is fine. (See attachment list below for suggested CSV layout.)
2) Confirm retention requirement (you mentioned ~90 days) and any export/audit obligations for longer-term storage.
3) Internal tech session: I'd like to schedule a 60-minute engineering demo with Ben Carter (solutions) and Karthik Iyer (security) to walk through masking options and a quick POC ingest of your sample logs. Proposed window: next week (Tue/Wed).

Attachments: redwood-sanitization-playbook-v1.pdf — short primer on our control types and onboarding checklist.

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and loop engineering. Appreciate the fast turnaround — we’ll treat this as a POC path for the pilot.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side and attaching an initial sanitized sample.

Clarifications:
- Retention: our compliance team requires 90 days of readily-queryable logs and an additional 2 years of archived metadata. For the pilot, we need to validate storage and export controls for the 90-day active window.
- Trace IDs: we consider internal trace IDs sensitive because they can be used to re-associate session activity; hashing is preferred to preserve cross-request correlation without keeping raw IDs.
- Required evidence: SOC2 overview + a short description of your redaction pipeline (how you guarantee non-reversibility).

We attached a 48-hour sample (carebridge-sample-logs-scrubbed.csv). Note: we redacted patient identifiers but left header shapes and example trace IDs (short tokens) so you can test hashing.

Can do engineering demo Wed or Thu next week (any time after 11am PT). We’d like to see: a) live ingest of the sample and b) redaction/hash configuration UI or examples, c) how sanitized logs are exported to our S3 or VPC.

Leaving Samantha on thread — she’ll be the compliance lead and will help with SOC/retention questions.

Thanks,

Priya / team —

Quick answers and proposed plan from solutions: 

Short answers:
- Hashing: yes — we support configurable hashing at ingest. We can do HMAC-SHA256 using a customer-managed KMS key (customer provides key ARN for Redwood Private, or we can reference a KMS-mapped key for Dedicated/Hosted with proof of key separation). Hashing is non-reversible when keys are not shared.
- Header filtering: drop/redact/hash by header name. Applies to both request and response headers.
- Retention: we can enforce TTLs per-tenant; 90-day active retention plus export/archive policy (S3 Glacier or customer-managed archive) is supported via our export rules. We can produce an audit trail showing redaction events.

Proposed POC (2-week fast path):
1) Wed 30 Jul / Thu 31 Jul — 60-min engineering demo (we’ll reserve Wed 11:30am PT; Priya please confirm). Demo will: ingest the attached CSV into a staging pipeline, apply a trace-id HMAC rule, show a sanitized CSV export, and demonstrate pushing sanitized stream to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket.
2) Within 48 hours after demo — we’ll provide the sanitized export and the redaction audit log.
3) If CareBridge wants, we can follow with a short security questionnaire (SOC2 pointer doc) and produce a scoped pilot contract for Redwood Private if they require customer-managed KMS and VPC-only access.
